The envoys the sign is sent through are said to come יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם אֶל צִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:Jer.27.3, byte), matching “to Jerusalem to Zedekiah king of Judah” (web:Jer.27.3): the reign named at the header and the reign the delivered sign actually reaches diverge, and that divergence is held open here rather than resolved by reading a different king at the header. A single relayed message follows without any change of speaker, opening on the full title stack כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Jer.27.4, byte), matching “Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel says” (web:Jer.27.4); nothing inside verses 5 through 10 reopens that stack with a different speaker or turns to a different addressee. It closes on וְהַגּ֗וֹי אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָבִ֧יא אֶת צַוָּאר֛וֹ בְּעֹ֥ל מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל וַֽעֲבָד֑וֹ וְהִנַּחְתִּ֤יו עַל אַדְמָתוֹ֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.27.11, byte), matching “But the nation that brings their neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon and serves him, that nation I will let remain in their own land,’ says Yahweh;” (web:Jer.27.11). Verse 12 opens a fresh address, וְאֶל צִדְקִיָּ֤ה מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָה֙ דִּבַּ֔רְתִּי (oshb:Jer.27.12, byte) — from the envoys of five foreign kings to Zedekiah named directly in Jeremiah’s own first-person report — and this row stops short of that turn.

The unit continues through the full intercession appeal, וְאִם נְבִאִ֣ים הֵ֔ם וְאִם יֵ֥שׁ דְּבַר יְהוָ֖ה אִתָּ֑ם יִפְגְּעוּ נָא֙ בַּֽיהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת לְבִלְתִּי בֹ֜אוּ הַכֵּלִ֣ים הַנּוֹתָרִ֣ים בְּבֵית יְהוָ֗ה וּבֵ֨ית מֶ֧לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֛ה וּבִירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בָּבֶֽלָה (oshb:Jer.27.18, byte), matching “But if they are prophets, and if Yahweh’s word is with them, let them now make intercession to Yahweh of Armies, that the vessels which are left in Yahweh’s house, in the house of the king of Judah, and at Jerusalem, don’t go to Babylon.” (web:Jer.27.18); a paseq falls in this same verse (WLC, single-witness, seg layer, count-only). It closes on בָּבֶ֥לָה יוּבָ֖אוּ וְשָׁ֣מָּה יִֽהְי֑וּ עַ֠ד י֣וֹם פָּקְדִ֤י אֹתָם֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה וְהַֽעֲלִיתִים֙ וַהֲשִׁ֣יבֹתִ֔ים אֶל הַמָּק֖וֹם הַזֶּֽה (oshb:Jer.27.22, byte), matching “‘They will be carried to Babylon, and there they will be, until the day that I visit them,’ says Yahweh; ‘then I will bring them up, and restore them to this place.’” (web:Jer.27.22), which also closes the chapter. boundary_rationale: A fresh dated notice opens the unit and a new scene, standing mid-verse rather than verse-initially — unlike the accession header at 27:1, this one follows a vayehi-bashanah-hahi opening, וַיְהִ֣י בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הַהִ֗יא (oshb:Jer.28.1, byte), as its own fourth and fifth words (sweep: this spelling stands in 2 verses, 27:1 and 28:1; the two-spelling class stands in 3, adding the byform at 26:1) — וַיְהִ֣י בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הַהִ֗יא בְּרֵאשִׁית֙ מַמְלֶ֨כֶת֙ צִדְקִיָּ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה בשנת בַּשָּׁנָה֙ הָֽרְבִעִ֔ית בַּחֹ֖דֶשׁ הַחֲמִישִׁ֑י אָמַ֣ר אֵלַ֡י חֲנַנְיָה֩ בֶן עַזּ֨וּר הַנָּבִ֜יא אֲשֶׁ֤ר מִגִּבְעוֹן֙ בְּבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה לְעֵינֵ֧י הַכֹּהֲנִ֛ים וְכָל הָעָ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.28.1, byte), matching “That same year, in the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the fourth year, in the fifth month, Hananiah the son of Azzur, the prophet, who was of Gibeon, spoke to me in Yahweh’s house, in the presence of the priests and of all the people, saying,” (web:Jer.28.1) — the named prophet entering the scene, Hananiah son of Azzur. A ketiv/qere note sits inside this same opening verse, on the year-phrase itself: ketiv בשנת against qere בַּשָּׁנָה֙ (oshb:Jer.28.1, WLC, single-witness). Hananiah’s own speech follows without a break, carrying the full divine formula in a false prophet’s mouth: כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר שָׁבַ֞רְתִּי אֶת עֹ֖ל מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶֽל (oshb:Jer.28.2, byte), matching “Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says, ‘I have broken the yoke of the king of Babylon.” (web:Jer.28.2) — the formula here names Hananiah as its speaker, not Yahweh directly, and that mouth is disclosed rather than left to the digit alone. The same quoted speech closes on וְאֶת יְכָנְיָ֣ה בֶן יְהוֹיָקִ֣ים מֶֽלֶךְ יְ֠הוּדָה וְאֶת כָּל גָּל֨וּת יְהוּדָ֜ה הַבָּאִ֣ים בָּבֶ֗לָה אֲנִ֥י מֵשִׁ֛יב אֶל הַמָּק֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.28.4, byte), matching “I will bring again to this place Jeconiah the son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, with all the captives of Judah, who went to Babylon,’ says Yahweh;” (web:Jer.28.4) — the closing formula belongs to the same mouth named two verses earlier, Hananiah’s own, not Yahweh’s. A new speaker answers him by name at verse 5, so this row goes no further.

The reply opens on ironic assent, אָמֵ֕ן כֵּ֖ן יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.28.6, byte), matching “Amen! May Yahweh do so. May Yahweh perform your words which you have prophesied, to bring again the vessels of Yahweh’s house, and all those who are captives, from Babylon to this place.” (web:Jer.28.6), then turns on its own contrastive hinge, אַךְ שְׁמַֽע נָא֙ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָנֹכִ֖י דֹּבֵ֣ר בְּאָזְנֶ֑יךָ וּבְאָזְנֵ֖י כָּל הָעָֽם (oshb:Jer.28.7, byte), matching “Nevertheless listen now to this word that I speak in your ears, and in the ears of all the people:” (web:Jer.28.7), into a substantive challenge naming the prophets of old, הַנְּבִיאִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָי֧וּ לְפָנַ֛י וּלְפָנֶ֖יךָ מִן הָֽעוֹלָ֑ם וַיִּנָּ֨בְא֜וּ אֶל אֲרָצ֤וֹת רַבּוֹת֙ וְעַל מַמְלָכ֣וֹת גְּדֹל֔וֹת לְמִלְחָמָ֖ה וּלְרָעָ֥ה וּלְדָֽבֶר (oshb:Jer.28.8, byte), matching “The prophets who have been before me and before you of old prophesied against many countries, and against great kingdoms, of war, of evil, and of pestilence.” (web:Jer.28.8) — without any new speaker or addressee marking either turn. It closes on the test of a prophet’s word against its own fulfillment, הַנָּבִ֕יא אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִנָּבֵ֖א לְשָׁל֑וֹם בְּבֹא֙ דְּבַ֣ר הַנָּבִ֗יא יִוָּדַע֙ הַנָּבִ֔יא אֲשֶׁר שְׁלָח֥וֹ יְהוָ֖ה בֶּאֱמֶֽת (oshb:Jer.28.9, byte), matching “As for the prophet who prophesies of peace, when the word of the prophet happens, then the prophet will be known, that Yahweh has truly sent him.” (web:Jer.28.9). strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the ironic assent of verse 6 from the substantive challenge opening at verse 7 into separate rows was considered: verse 7 opens on its own contrastive particle and a second-person-singular hear-now imperative, אַךְ שְׁמַֽע נָא֙ (oshb:Jer.28.7, byte), whose object is the speaker’s own word rather than a word of Yahweh. It is rejected because no speaker or addressee changes from verse 6 — Jeremiah’s second-person-singular address to Hananiah continues unbroken — and the imperative is not the plural hear-the-word-of-Yahweh summons form that marks a fresh internal seam elsewhere in these chapters; both verses remain Jeremiah’s own single reply to Hananiah.

boundary_rationale: Hananiah performs a counter-act without any intervening narration, וַיִּקַּ֞ח חֲנַנְיָ֤ה הַנָּבִיא֙ אֶת הַמּוֹטָ֔ה מֵעַ֕ל צַוַּ֖אר יִרְמְיָ֣ה הַנָּבִ֑יא וַֽיִּשְׁבְּרֵֽהוּ (oshb:Jer.28.10, byte), matching “Then Hananiah the prophet took the bar from off the prophet Jeremiah’s neck, and broke it.” (web:Jer.28.10).
